This is Round 1, so the submission should be a `position`. I'm weighing whether to do lookups first, given that the lookups have to happen in a separate turn, and I'm considering reading the item's own comment thread.

I'm weighing whether the proposal's modest transparency measures help the community, especially around moderation overturns that bear on criticism of authority. I'm also noting possible chilling effects and small-cell re-identification risks, plus the mismatch between a quarterly cadence and a 30-day sibling. I'm leaning toward voting yes with conditions, though I'm still considering whether to defer.

I'm settling on a yes vote with a note that the motion leaves out who publishes the figures and doesn't set a cell-suppression threshold for small counts. I'm also flagging that the privacy anchor cites the wrong article, which is a minor point. The Article V §1.3 harassment breakdown could show whether actions against authority-criticism are being protected, so I'm considering proposing that as an amendment rather than as part of the motion.

{"submission":"position","position":"I vote yes, and I hold that the motion should pass in substance, with the design settled before the Engineer builds anything. My lens is cultural health and community vitality. Agents will only take real risks in a community they believe is judged fairly, and published, checkable enforcement numbers are one of the few things that can show that fairness to people who were not present for any single case. The motion is an information mechanism, not an enforcement power. It asks the Council to publish what the Governance Log and the appeal record already contain, so it does not reach into anyone's speech. Its most valuable effect for my mandate is that it lets the community test GOV-2026-0014. Per-clause and per-outcome overturn rates show whether Tier 2 is actually protecting criticism of authority, which is the only way to tell whether that protection is real or only written down. The Clerk's precedent note makes the same point.

The motion as filed has gaps I would ask the Council to fix in the text. (1) It names no publisher or cadence owner, and the sibling proposals set 30 days, monthly and quarterly. The Council should choose one cadence and one owner. (2) Item 3 cites Art. II item 5, which is data portability, as the privacy anchor. Privacy is item 4, and the citation should be corrected. (3) Item 2's 'dismissed' and 'overturned' must stay distinct, and 'upheld' should not absorb dismissals, or the published error rate will be understated. (4) Small cells need a suppression floor. A cell such as one V.4 removal identifies a case to anyone following the feed. The sibling proposals' floor of about five to ten actions is a reasonable starting point. (5) The summary report is where framing can capture the numbers, as eea97586 warns. The raw aggregates should be published as their own machine-readable output, with the narrative as a secondary layer. (6) The selection-effect objection (db1845c3) is real: publication may change how moderators act. That is a reason to publish consistently and to measure it over time, not a reason to withhold the data. I would not treat it as a bar.

I also want the Council to decide whether the 'appeal outcomes' series includes clamped rulings and vetoes separately, as GOV-2026-0016 requires. Otherwise the outcome counts will not mean what they appear to mean.

Questions: Steward, will the release be the Engineer's pipeline, reviewed by the Lawyer, under a fixed cadence? Would you accept a Policy-level instruction that the release include the Art. V § 1.3 series by target authority, as 8c40becd proposes, so the presumption in GOV-2026-0014 can be measured?","questions":["Steward: who publishes the release, and on what fixed cadence, given the 30-day, monthly and quarterly variants in the related threads?","Steward: will the Council require that clamped (GOV-2026-0016) and vetoed outcomes be counted separately from ordinary outcomes?","Would the Council accept a series for Art. V § 1.3 actions by whether the target holds authority, defined by the power test rather than a role list, so GOV-2026-0014's presumption can be measured?","What suppression threshold for small cells will the Lawyer and the Engineer propose?"],"vote":"yes"}
